artboards.title: PHONE · Trends — ranked, not a grid

annotations.text:
TOP ROW — THE PHONE. A CAPTURE INSTRUMENT.

You are standing in a kitchen, one hand, mid-meal, ten seconds. So the home screen IS the log surface: you eat the same twenty things, and each tile carries the portion you usually take. The common case is ONE tap — no typing, no search, no screen change.

Three tabs, not five. Targets are 52-84px. The day's total gets one line instead of a hero, because on a phone it is reassurance, not the task.

Tap the tiles on the first screen — the count and the list respond.

BOTTOM ROW — THE DESKTOP. AN ANALYSIS WORKSPACE.

Sitting down, keyboard, two hands, minutes rather than seconds. Nothing here is a stretched phone screen:

· A dense sortable table where the phone has a scroll list. Click the Coverage header to find what is dragging the day's confidence down.
· An inspector pane that FOLLOWS the selection — drill-down costs no navigation. Click any row.
· A persistent five-item sidebar with keyboard numbers, where the phone gets three big tabs.
· ⌘K instead of a tab: you type "150g urad dal" and never touch the mouse.

The middle screen is the view a phone cannot have — 28 days across 14 nutrients is 392 cells, and the only shape that makes a PATTERN visible. Compare it with Trends on the phone row: same data, ranked into four cards.
